passages.text: The following discussion includes results of operations and financial condition for the fiscal year ended November 1, 2025 (fiscal 2025) and the fiscal year ended November 2, 2024 (fiscal 2024) and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. For discussion on results of operations and financial condition for fiscal 2024 and the fiscal year ended October 28, 2023 (fiscal 2023) and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023, please refer to Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 26, 2024. Our fiscal year is the 52-week or 53-week period ending on the Saturday closest to the last day in October. Fiscal 2025 was a 52-week fiscal period, while fiscal 2024 was a 53-week fiscal period. The additional week in fiscal 2024 was included in the first quarter ended February 3, 2024. Therefore, fiscal 2025 includes one less week of operations as compared to fiscal 2024. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Set forth below and elsewhere in this report are descriptions of certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements in this report. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we presently deem less significant may also adversely affect our business. For more information, see the section titled “Note About Forward-Looking Statements” of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Risks Related to our Business, Operations, Industry and Partners Global political and economic uncertainty and adverse conditions related to our international operations could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. We have significant operations and manufacturing facilities outside the United States, including in Ireland, the Philippines, Thailand and Malaysia. A significant portion of our revenue is derived from customers in international markets, and we expect that international sales will continue to account for a significant portion of our revenue in the future. As a result of our international operations, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be negatively impacted by, among others, the following factors: • political, legal and economic changes, crises or instability and civil unrest that may impact markets in which we do business, such as macroeconomic weakness related to trade and political disputes between the United States and Europe or China, tensions across the Taiwan Strait that may adversely affect our operations in Taiwan, our customers and the technology industry supply chain, and the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine and tensions in Israel and the Middle East; • trade policy, commercial, travel, export or taxation disputes or restrictions, import, export or sector-based tariffs, changes to export classifications or other restrictions imposed by the U.S. government or by the governments of the countries in which we do business, particularly with respect to China; • compliance requirements of customs and export regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations and the International Traffic and Arms Regulations; • currency conversion risks and exchange rate and interest rate fluctuations and uncertainty; • instability of global credit and financial markets due to uncertainty and adverse macroeconomic conditions such as inflation, tariffs and trade restrictions, high interest rates, bank failures and slower economic growth or recession that could, among other impacts, affect our ability to timely access external financing sources on acceptable terms or lead to financial difficulties or uncertainty of our customers, suppliers and distributors exposing us to late payments, cancelled orders and inventory challenges; • sanctions imposed by the U.S. government or by the governments in countries in which we do business, which could adversely impact our business by preventing us from performing existing contracts, recognizing revenue, pursuing new business opportunities or receiving payment for products already supplied to customers; credit_strengths.text: Operating margin expanded sharply year over year and sits well above the sector median, reflecting pricing power and a richer mix across Industrial, Automotive and Communications end markets. This profitability cushion underpins cash generation through the cycle and supports internal funding of capital spending.

Free cash flow comfortably covers dividends and buybacks combined, so shareholder returns are funded from internally generated cash rather than incremental borrowing. Operating cash flow also exceeds capital expenditure plus dividends, leaving residual liquidity for debt reduction or bolt-on acquisitions.

key_risks.text: The issuer discloses material exposure to international operations and manufacturing in Ireland, the Philippines, Thailand and Malaysia, plus trade, tariff and export-control risk particularly with respect to China. Such disruptions could compress revenue and margins, weakening the cash flow that currently services debt.

Gross leverage sits modestly above the sector median and debt has risen each year in the trend series, even as net leverage improved on stronger earnings. A demand reversal in cyclical end markets would lift leverage toward the next risk band, narrowing headroom that is currently adequate but not ample.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year over year and remains strong in absolute terms, though it trails the sector median, indicating a comparatively heavier debt load relative to operating profit. Coverage is nonetheless sufficient to absorb a meaningful earnings decline without impairing debt service.

Free cash flow to debt improved year over year and marginally exceeds the sector median, while operating cash flow to debt trails peers. Liquidity is solid, with a current ratio above both the prior year and the sector median, and cash balances provide a meaningful offset to gross borrowings.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Minimal, with net leverage on a cash-and-short-investment basis well inside the next risk-band boundary and cash flow coverage similarly strong. Our judgement is that the balance sheet can absorb a moderate earnings downturn before leverage becomes a rating-relevant concern.

Debt is predominantly long-dated, with only a small short-term borrowing component and no current maturities of long-term debt, so refinancing concentration is limited. We view the maturity profile as comfortable, though continued buybacks and dividends absorb most free cash flow and constrain deleveraging pace.

credit_strengths.text: 營業利潤率按年大幅擴張，並顯著高於行業中位數，反映定價能力以及工業、汽車和通訊終端市場的更豐富產品組合。此盈利能力緩衝支撐整個週期的現金生成，並支持資本開支的內部融資。
自由現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋股息和回購的總和，因此股東回報由內部產生的現金而非增量借貸提供資金。經營現金流亦超過資本開支加股息，留下剩餘流動性用於減債或補強型收購。

key_risks.text: 發行人披露在愛爾蘭、菲律賓、泰國和馬來西亞的國際業務和製造方面存在重大風險敞口，以及貿易、關稅和出口管制風險，尤其是對中國的風險。此類中斷可能壓縮收入和利潤率，削弱目前用於償債的現金流。
總槓桿略高於行業中位數，且在趨勢序列中債務逐年上升，儘管淨槓桿因盈利增強而改善。週期性終端市場的需求逆轉將使槓桿升至下一個風險區間，收窄目前充足但並不寬裕的緩衝空間。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善，絕對水平仍然強勁，但低於行業中位數，表明相對於經營利潤的債務負擔較重。儘管如此，覆蓋率足以吸收有意義的盈利下降而不損害償債能力。
自由現金流對債務比率按年改善並略高於行業中位數，而經營現金流對債務比率落後於同業。流動性穩健，流動比率高於上年和行業中位數，現金餘額對總借款提供有意義的抵銷。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，以現金及短期投資為基礎的淨槓桿遠在下一個風險區間邊界之內，現金流覆蓋率同樣強勁。我們的判斷是，資產負債表可吸收溫和的盈利下滑，之後槓桿才成為與評級相關的關注點。
債務主要為長期，短期借款部分很小，且長期債務無流動到期，因此再融資集中度有限。我們認為到期結構舒適，儘管持續回購和股息吸收大部分自由現金流並制約去槓桿步伐。
